metadata.hardware_requirements: computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic data including volumes from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China. Used for simulation calibration and agent training.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Paper explicitly states data used is available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract vehicle locations and construct position matrices
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations (xi, yi) are extracted from video frames to create a sparse binary matrix of size X by Y. This is then supplemented with signal state info and down-sampled to size 4 x 512.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, some tool specifics (object detector) missing, dimensions for input matrix defined but sampling rate not fully detailed.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st.
nodes_process.description: Stacks N consecutive position matrices to capture traffic dynamics. For this study, N=3 frames are stacked.

nodes_process.node_name: DRL Model Training via Multitask Learning
nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: Trains a modified DRL (DQN) with multitasking. Uses Adam optimizer to minimize a loss function combining Q-value error and predictive error for mean speed and queue length. Uses experience replay and a frozen target network for stability.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, almost all hyperparameters and architecture details listed in Table 1 and Fig 7.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO... in comparison with a state-of-the-practice method
nodes_process.description: Evaluation on the Qingdao-Huangdao tunnel road network using SUMO simulator. Compare proposed DRL against 'No Control' and PI-ALINEA baselines. Reports convergence, travel times, speeds, and queue lengths.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, evaluation hardware and simulation environment parameters specified.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Plots the convergence of episode rewards and mean travel time during the training phase over one million frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Inputs based on cited SUMO simulator and real-world traffic data; methodology mostly specified, but precise simulator seed values not provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box-and-whisker plot comparing mainline vehicle travel times for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL across a time period (8:00 to 9:00).
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Based on cited simulator and specific volume data (Fig 6); parameters for baseline PI-ALINEA provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps (contour plots) showing speed distributions over distance and time for three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Requires spatial simulation setup from Fig 5 and 6; methods are described but contour generation details omitted.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series plot showing on-ramp queue lengths (quartiles) for different control methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Direct output from calibrated SUMO simulation; clear correspondence with described scenario constraints.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12: Relationship of queue length and red ratio for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plots and regression lines showing the correlation between the ramp signal's red ratio and the resulting queue length for two methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Relies on logging signal state-to-result mapping; precise mapping of 'red ratio' calculation slightly ambiguous.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots showing the distribution of traffic volume (veh/h) downstream of the merging area at 5-minute intervals for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Straightforward aggregation of simulator output using provided volume inputs (Fig 6).

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Sensitivity analysis (perturbation analysis) showing mainline travel time across different spatial subarea data occlusions.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear methodology for masking specific subareas defined in Fig 15; leverages the primary simulation pipeline.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of mean travel times (seconds) and percentage changes across 20 trials for No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Lists raw results for individual random seeds, although seeds themselves aren't explicitly provided.
